arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Call argued Johnson's conviction rests on minimal contact. She stated this does not qualify as a violent felony. She emphasized the state law's broad scope.
Ms. Kruger argued the federal definition matches the state law. She cited the unlawful application of physical force. She asserted the state crime fits the federal statute.
Justice Alito asked how to determine the necessary force level. He noted any touching involves some physical force. He sought a clear standard for the federal statute.
Justice Ginsburg questioned the record regarding the specific conduct. She noted the state plea did not detail the actions. She asked if state law typing matters for the federal analysis.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case asks if a Florida battery conviction counts as a violent felony. the side that brought the case argues the state law allows conviction for minimal contact. The government argues the federal statute matches the state definition. The Court must decide if the state crime fits the federal definition.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on October 6, 2009.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Johnson wants the Court to reject the enhanced sentence. He argues the state law allows conviction for minimal contact. He seeks a sentence based only on the current offense.
The United States wants the Court to uphold the enhanced sentence. It argues the state law matches the federal definition. It seeks to treat the prior conviction as a violent felony.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Johnson argues the state statute allows conviction for the slightest contact. He claims this minimal force does not meet the federal standard. He asserts the state law is broader than the federal definition.
The United States argues the federal statute tracks the state definition. It claims the unlawful application of force fits the federal text. It asserts the state crime is a violent felony.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Breyer asked why the parties view the issues as separate. He questioned the distinction between the state and federal definitions.
Justice Scalia noted the prior offense elevated the current charge. He asked if the Court needs to know what is normal. He questioned the necessity of defining normal conduct levels.
